q7.answer: Workers read billing_mode at the start of every run, so they pick up a change only on the first run that starts after the audited write. A run already in progress finishes in the mode it started in, and the new engine checks the provider by idempotency key before any charge, so an invoice caught mid-change is not charged twice.

q8.answer: The evidence sits in the rollout record in the billing store: daily comparison results, the shadow streak, unresolved mismatches, and the Finance sign-off with approver and time. The system checks these gates when the audited mode-change write arrives and refuses the write if a gate is unmet or the kill switch is set, so a person cannot promote early by simply writing the flag.

q9.answer: The rollout controller evaluates every 10-minute window of new-engine charge attempts and failures, which the charge path writes to the rollout record, and it computes failed attempts divided by all attempts. When the rate is above 2% in both or new_only, it starts the rollback steps, beginning with freeze_moves, and never writes billing_mode. What the controller physically is (a service, a scheduled job, or part of the workers) is not decided.

q10.answer: Charges that fall due during rollback are held in their attempt records, not dropped, because the kill switch stops both engines from charging in ordinary runs. They are actually made only in resume_old, after reconciliation and any replay are complete, on-call has written billing_mode to old_only, and the old engine charges each unowned or not-yet-charged period once under its key before the switch is cleared.

q11.answer: Each charge is keyed by customer ID plus billing period ID, and the key is recorded before the first provider call, so both engines identify the same charge. Reconciliation checks the provider by key and marks every period the new engine already charged as owned by it, and resume_old charges only unowned or not-yet-charged periods, with the kill switch blocking ordinary runs in the meantime. Safety still depends on the provider treating repeated same-key calls as one charge, which is an open point to confirm.

q12.answer: Billing is left frozen: the kill switch stays set, billing_mode is unchanged, forward moves are refused, and ordinary runs make no charges or ledger writes. Each step is idempotent and the rollout record notes the last completed step, so re-running the rollback resumes from there. Which component restarts an interrupted rollback is not decided, because the controller's form is still open.
